clinical.citation: ASHG 2018 - Systematic scoring of candidate genes for neurodevelopmental disorders has a higher yield than large meta-analyses (Jamra et al.)

variants.description: Not specified; FBXL19 listed among top-scoring candidate genes with potentially causative variants in trio exome sequencing of undiagnosed NDD cases

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Candidate gene variant prioritized by a 13-parameter scoring system (inheritance, gene and variant attributes, literature); FBXL19 was in the top 10% of scores. No variant-level detail is provided.
clinical.center_country: Germany (Leipzig/Jamra group, with collaborating German centers; exome sequencing by Centogene, Rostock, and CeGaT, Tübingen)

model_organism.citation: Williamson et al. 2018 - FBXL19 recruits CDK-Mediator to CpG islands of developmental genes priming them for activation during lineage commitment (PMID: 29809150)
phenotypes: Recognition of CpG islands by FBXL19 (via its CxxC zinc finger domain) is reported to be essential for mouse development
The abstract does not give details of the in vivo phenotype (e.g. the stage of developmental failure)
In ES cells, loss of FBXL19 CpG island binding impairs CDK-Mediator recruitment to developmental gene promoters and priming of these genes for activation during lineage commitment

model_organism.citation: Posttranslational regulation of CREB-binding protein expression by F-box leucine-rich repeat-containing protein 19 and ubiquitin-specific peptidase 14 in the paraventricular nucleus participates in chronic stress-induced symptomatology via the modulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (PMID: 41028568)
phenotypes: Genetic knockdown of FBXL19 in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of naive mice mimicked chronic stress and produced a similar symptomatology
This was mediated by increased CRH biosynthesis, which required the CBP-CREB interaction and CBP acetyltransferase activity
Genetic knockout of FBXL19 aggravated chronic stress-induced symptomatology (depression-like/neuropsychiatric behaviors)
Overexpression of FBXL19 or TAT-FBXL19 infusion in the PVN reversed chronic stress-induced symptomatology
Chronic social defeat stress and chronic unpredictable mild stress altered the FBXL19-USP14-CBP system in the PVN

biological.citation: Turberfield et al. 2019 - FBXL19 recruits CDK-Mediator to CpG islands of developmental genes priming them for activation during lineage commitment (PMID: 29809150)
biological.summary: FBXL19 was identified as a CpG island-binding protein in mouse ES cells that associates with the CDK-Mediator complex. It recruits CDK-Mediator to CpG island promoters of non-transcribed developmental genes, priming them for activation during lineage commitment. CpG island recognition by FBXL19 is essential for mouse development.

biological.citation: Identification and characterization of FBXL19 gene in silico (PMID: 15547684)
biological.summary: Bioinformatic identification of human FBXL19 (CXXC11) as a 674-aa protein encoded by 10 exons at 16p11.2, paralogous to FBXL10 and FBXL11 and sharing the FBXHA (containing CXXC) and FBXHB (containing F-box) domains. Human FBXL19 shows 97.5% amino-acid identity with mouse Fbxl19.

biological.citation: FBXL19 in endothelial cells protects the heart from influenza A infection by enhancing antiviral immunity and reducing cellular senescence programs (PMID: 39150394)
biological.summary: In a mouse model of influenza A infection, EC-specific FBXL19 overexpression reduced viral titers and M1 protein. It increased IFN-α/β/γ and RANTES, restored IRF3 protein (not mRNA) levels, and reduced cardiac inflammation. It also partially reversed IAV-induced senescence markers (p16/p21 up, lamin-B1 down).

biological.citation: Epigenetic Regulation of Immune and Inflammatory Responses in Rheumatoid Arthritis (PMID: 35479077)
biological.summary: An integrative epigenetic network analysis of RA datasets (GEO) identified FBXL19 as one of five hub genes (with CHD3, SETD1B, SMARCA4, SETD1A) associated with immune cells and inflammatory responses.

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies additional susceptibility loci for psoriasis
biological.summary: A meta-GWAS of three European cohorts showed support for the FBXL19 locus as a known psoriasis susceptibility locus.

biological.citation: The pathogenesis and genetics of psoriasis (PMID: 23369832)
biological.summary: This review places FBXL19 among psoriasis-associated genes involved in innate immune responses and NF-κB signaling, together with TNFAIP3, TNIP1, NFKBIA, REL, TYK2, NOS2 and CARD14.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Glucocorticoids unmask silent non-coding genetic risk variants for common diseases
biological.summary: Obesity-associated SNPs mediated cortisol-responsive (glucocorticoid receptor-dependent) expression of FBXL19, described as an adipogenesis-controlling gene, in a GR-mediated eQTL analysis in B-lymphoblastoid cell lines.

biological.citation: Long Noncoding RNA FBXL19-AS1 Expedites Cell Growth, Migration and Invasion in Cervical Cancer by miR-193a-5p/PIN1 Signaling (PMID: 33116834)
biological.summary: The antisense lncRNA FBXL19-AS1 is upregulated in cervical cancer. It sponges miR-193a-5p to raise PIN1 expression, and its knockdown reduces proliferation, migration and invasion and induces apoptosis. This concerns the antisense lncRNA rather than the FBXL19 protein.

biological.citation: LIN28A-stabilized FBXL19-AS1 promotes breast cancer migration, invasion and EMT by regulating WDR66 (PMID: 31140103)
biological.summary: FBXL19-AS1 interacts with and is stabilized by the RNA-binding protein LIN28A (RIP assay) and promotes WDR66 expression, driving breast cancer migration, invasion and EMT.

biological.citation: Analysis of associations of FBXL19-AS1 with occurrence, development and prognosis of acute pancreatitis (PMID: 33378025)
biological.summary: Serum FBXL19-AS1 is elevated in severe acute pancreatitis and predicts severity (AUC 0.9177). Overexpression upregulated IL-1β, TNF-α and IL-6 mRNA in AP cells, and knockdown had the opposite effect.
